hero.headline: Trump calls court system rigged after rulings block tariffs and Kennedy Center renaming
hero.body:
Trump wrote on Truth Social that the court system is rigged, comparing it unfavorably to the judicial systems in other countries. The statement came after courts ruled against a key part of his economic policy and blocked the addition of his name to the Kennedy Center.

The rulings represent setbacks for the administration's agenda. One decision halted implementation of tariff policies that Trump had described as central to his economic plans. The other stopped the renaming of the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts to include the president's name.

Trump's criticism of the judiciary echoes previous statements he has made about courts that rule against his policies. The president has repeatedly questioned the impartiality of judges who issue unfavorable decisions.

The tariff ruling affects trade policy that the administration had sought to implement as part of its broader economic strategy. The court found legal issues with how the tariffs were being imposed, though Trump maintained the policies were necessary for American economic interests.

The Kennedy Center decision addressed efforts to rename the Washington cultural institution. The venue has hosted performances and events since 1971 and is named after President John F. Kennedy. Courts blocked the proposed name change.

White House Communications Director Steven Cheung has defended the president's policies in other matters, calling criticism of administration decisions fake news. The administration has not yet announced whether it will appeal either ruling.

The decisions add to a series of legal challenges the administration has faced in implementing its policy priorities. Federal courts have acted as a check on executive actions across multiple policy areas.

Trump characterized the rulings as evidence of bias in the judicial system. He argued that courts were preventing him from fulfilling campaign promises to voters. Legal experts note that judicial review of executive actions is a standard part of the constitutional system of checks and balances.

cards.headline: Trump weighs decision on Iran deal as conflict enters third month
cards.body:
President Trump is working to reach a nuclear agreement with Iran as the conflict intensifies militarily. Trump said it will become clear within "probably 10 days" whether a deal is possible, speaking at the inaugural meeting of his Board of Peace in Washington DC. He insisted that Iran cannot possess nuclear weapons and warned that "bad things will happen" if the country continues to threaten regional stability.

White House envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Iranian officials in Geneva to discuss Iran's nuclear enrichment program. The program was set back but not eliminated following US and Israeli bombing during a 12-day military campaign last June. After the diplomatic meeting, Iran promised to respond within two weeks to US demands that it abandon enrichment entirely in exchange for sanctions relief, roughly matching Trump's stated timeline.

However, Trump's track record on Iran timing raises questions. Last summer, he gave himself two weeks to decide whether to bomb Iran's underground nuclear enrichment facility at Fordow before striking it with B-2 stealth bombers within days.

The military buildup in the region continues even as negotiations proceed. A second carrier strike group, led by the USS Gerald R Ford, is heading to the Middle East. Experts say the US already has sufficient military assets in the region to conduct an aerial bombing campaign against Iran, potentially coordinated with Israel, though the strategic outcome of such action remains unclear.

The prolonged conflict is taking a toll on the US economy and Trump's political standing. US inflation rose at its fastest pace in three years in April, driven by higher energy prices from the war. Americans are growing frustrated with Trump's economic management, with his approval rating falling to nearly its lowest level since returning to the White House. A Reuters/Ipsos survey showed declining support among Republicans specifically.

Energy costs are rising for millions of households. Under the regulator's new price cap, a household using typical energy amounts will pay 221 pounds more annually. The war is estimated to cost 2 billion dollars per day, with experts projecting a final price tag of at least a trillion dollars.

Critics argue Trump is undermining his own negotiations. One analysis noted that "the self-proclaimed master dealmaker can't seem to stop sabotaging his own negotiations or acknowledge that Iran is now in a better position to demand concessions than it was before the war."

Trump skipped his eldest son's wedding in the Bahamas and canceled weekend plans at his New Jersey golf club, heightening speculation he was preparing to announce a deal. He announced a cabinet meeting for Wednesday, though no agreement has been announced yet.

The negotiations represent Trump's effort to declare victory and move past the conflict before it causes further economic damage and harms Republican chances in midterm elections.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth softens China rhetoric at Singapore conference
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth moderated his tone on China while speaking to Pacific leaders weeks after President Trump met with Chinese officials in Beijing.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth adopted a more moderate tone on China during his remarks at the Shangri-La Dialogue conference in Singapore, a shift occurring weeks after President Trump's bilateral summit in Beijing. While acknowledging "rightful alarm" over China's military buildup, Hegseth notably avoided discussing Taiwan in his address to Pacific leaders and diplomats.

Hegseth urged Asian allies to increase their military spending and take on greater responsibility for regional security. His balanced approach reflected an effort to manage U.S.-China relations while encouraging greater burden-sharing among America's regional partners against emerging threats.

cards.headline: China advances in drug development, challenging US dominance
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotechnology industry expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Chinese pharmaceutical research is gaining prominence at an international oncology gathering in Chicago, where clinical trials from Chinese companies are featured alongside traditional Western research. The country's biotechnology sector has grown substantially in recent years, supported by government investment and an expanding research infrastructure.

The rise of Chinese drug development has prompted concern among US industry leaders about potential shifts in global pharmaceutical leadership. China now conducts a significant portion of global clinical trials and has developed its own pipeline of experimental treatments, particularly in oncology.

cards.headline: Colombia's presidential election tests leftist strength in Latin America
cards.teaser: A leftist candidate leads in polls ahead of Colombia's presidential vote, but a far-right challenger has gained ground.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential election represents a crucial moment for the political left across Latin America. The leftist candidate leads in polls, but faces a strong challenge from a far-right outsider known as "The Tiger," who has gained significant momentum in recent weeks.

The election takes place amid a resurgence of political violence tied to Colombia's decades-long armed conflict. The contest reflects broader divisions between left and right over how to address the ongoing struggles involving the army, paramilitaries, and dissident factions of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo kills over 245
cards.body:
More than 245 suspected cases of Ebola have been reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province, with confirmed deaths reaching at least 65 people. The outbreak has prompted urgent international attention as health officials and aid organizations mobilize to contain the spread of this rare and dangerous virus.

The World Health Organization chief has arrived in Congo's capital to support containment efforts. The WHO estimates the death rate from this outbreak at between 30 to 50 percent among confirmed cases. "It's huge. It means that up to five out of 10 people are likely to die," said Anaïs Legand from the WHO's high threat pathogens team.

Médecins Sans Frontières has raised alarm about the outbreak's rapid progression. The charity warned that no previous Ebola outbreak has recorded so many cases so soon after being declared, highlighting the unusual speed at which this epidemic is spreading compared to past incidents.

The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, a particularly concerning development. The Democratic Republic of Congo's national research laboratory detected the virus in 13 of 20 samples tested. Unlike the Zaire strain of Ebola, for which vaccines exist, there is currently no licensed vaccine for the Bundibugyo variant. Only two previous outbreaks of this strain have occurred, in 2007 and 2012.

Cases have been reported mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also appearing in the neighboring city of Bunia. The Ituri province, which borders Uganda and South Sudan, is home to mining towns with significant population movement, creating challenges for disease control efforts. Uganda's health ministry has confirmed an outbreak in the country after a 59-year-old man died in a Kampala hospital following travel from the DRC.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has expressed concern about further spread across the region. The organization has called an urgent meeting with authorities from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, along with the WHO and pharmaceutical companies, to coordinate response efforts.

Health workers in the region face particular challenges as they treat patients with limited medical equipment and protective resources. The Democratic Republic of Congo has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976. Experts point to multiple factors contributing to recurring outbreaks, including close contact with animal reservoirs such as bats and primates, movement between rural and urban areas, and the region's tropical climate and rainforest environment.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with body fluids including blood and vomit from infected people, as well as during funeral preparation rituals. The disease causes severe illness with high fatality rates.

cards.headline: SpaceX prepares $80 billion IPO with most shares already allocated
cards.teaser: SpaceX is planning an initial public offering valued at $80 billion, but the majority of shares have already been committed to specific buyers.
cards.body:
SpaceX is proceeding with an $80 billion IPO, though 78 percent of the offering has already been allocated to existing investors, significantly limiting shares available to retail buyers. The company revealed in its IPO filing that government contracts already represent one-fifth of its 2025 revenue, including a recent $6.45 billion Space Force contract award.

The structure creates a challenging situation for Wall Street firms, which risk losing future business if they don't participate, while their clients face limited upside potential given the high valuation and pre-sold shares. This mirrors a broader trend of technology companies going public at valuations that offer minimal room for post-IPO gains.

cards.headline: Drone hits Romanian apartment building as war spills across border
cards.teaser: A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, underscoring risks the Russia-Ukraine war poses to neighboring countries.
cards.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania early Friday morning, causing an explosion and fire. Romania's government says the drone was likely hit by Ukrainian air defences while over Ukraine, which altered its trajectory before it crossed into Romanian territory. NATO and the EU condemned Russia over the incident.

Residents have begun returning to check on their homes in the affected building. The strike underscores how the Russia-Ukraine war poses direct threats to civilian areas in neighboring NATO member states, leaving residents fearful about their safety.

cards.headline: NATO territory hit by Russian drone, raising questions about alliance defenses
cards.teaser: The failure to intercept a Russian drone before it struck Romania has increased anxiety about NATO solidarity and collective defense commitments.
cards.body:
A Russian drone struck a residential building in Romania early Friday morning, damaging civilian infrastructure. Romanian officials believe the drone was hit by air defenses over Ukraine, which altered its trajectory before it crossed into NATO territory.

The incident has shaken residents, with people only beginning to return and assess damage to their homes. The breach of NATO airspace has raised broader concerns about the alliance's ability to protect member states and fueled questions about collective defense commitments.

cards.headline: Colombia's presidential election tests leftist strength in Latin America
cards.teaser: A leftist candidate leads in polls ahead of Colombia's presidential vote, but a far-right challenger has gained ground.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential election represents a crucial moment for the political left across Latin America. The leftist candidate leads in polls, but faces a strong challenge from a far-right outsider known as "The Tiger," who has gained significant momentum in recent weeks.

The election takes place amid a resurgence of political violence tied to Colombia's decades-long armed conflict. The contest reflects broader divisions between left and right over how to address the ongoing struggles involving the army, paramilitaries, and dissident factions of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia.

cards.headline: Truck crash kills 22 returning refugees in eastern Afghanistan
cards.teaser: A truck carrying refugees back to Afghanistan crashed in the eastern part of the country, killing 22 people.
cards.body:
Twenty-two people died when a truck transporting returning refugees crashed in eastern Afghanistan. The vehicle was carrying individuals who had been living outside the country and were traveling back.

The crash adds to the dangers facing displaced Afghans attempting to return home. Afghanistan has seen large numbers of refugees in neighboring countries, with periodic returns occurring under difficult and often unsafe conditions.

cards.headline: Trump weighs decision on Iran war deal as Middle East awaits outcome
cards.teaser: President Trump said he will soon make a final determination on whether to proceed with an agreement to end the war with Iran.
cards.body:
President Trump has wavered on whether to move forward with an agreement with Iran to end ongoing hostilities. He stated he would make a final determination soon, leaving the Middle East in a state of anticipation about the direction of U.S. policy.

The president's indecision has kept regional actors uncertain about whether diplomacy will succeed in halting the conflict. The potential deal would represent a significant shift in U.S.-Iran relations, but Trump has not committed publicly to accepting its terms.

cards.headline: Iranian soccer team practices in Turkey while awaiting U.S. visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: Iran's national soccer team is training in Turkey and developing backup plans as visa approvals for travel to the United States remain pending.
cards.body:
The Iranian national soccer team continues training in Turkey while awaiting U.S. visa approvals needed to compete in the World Cup. The delay has created uncertainty around the team's participation in the tournament.

Players are preparing backup plans in case visa authorization does not arrive in time, with diplomatic complications overshadowing their athletic preparations for the competition.

cards.headline: Sheriff's deputy killed in Virginia shooting, suspect at large
cards.teaser: A Carroll County sheriff's deputy was killed and another injured during a welfare check, prompting a manhunt.
cards.body:
A Carroll County sheriff's deputy died after being shot while conducting a welfare check. A second deputy was injured in the incident. The suspect fled the scene and remained at large.

The US Marshals Service offered a reward for information leading to the suspect's arrest. Carroll County officials confirmed the shooting and said a search was underway for the person accused of killing the deputy.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump administration plan to rename and close Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge stopped the administration's effort to renovate and rename the Kennedy Center in Washington.
cards.body:
A federal judge ruled that the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts must retain its name honoring President John F. Kennedy. In a 94-page decision, the judge wrote that it was "crystal clear" the arts complex was named after the late president.

The ruling also blocked the Trump administration's plan to close the center for two years of renovations. The judge prevented the venue from winding down its programming at this time.

cards.headline: Justice Department requests judge's recusal in Georgia election case
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors asked a judge to step aside from the case after reports the judge attended an event involving Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis.
cards.body:
I appreciate you providing the additional materials, but I notice the sources provided don't contain relevant details about the Georgia election case recusal motion mentioned in the original card.

The Guardian article discusses a Trump IRS lawsuit in Miami, the NPR headline references mail-in voting and Israel-Lebanon talks, and the AP News reference is cited but not provided in full text. None of these sources contain information about the judge's attendance at a Fulton County District Attorney event or the specific details of the DOJ's recusal motion in the Georgia election case.

Since I cannot verify the original card's claims against the provided source material, I'm returning the original text unchanged:

The Department of Justice filed a motion seeking the recusal of a judge presiding over a Georgia election case. The request came after reports that the judge attended an event associated with Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis.

The recusal motion raises questions about potential conflicts of interest in the case. The judge has not yet ruled on the Justice Department's request to step aside from the proceedings.

cards.headline: Catholic priest convicted of sexually assaulting women in Texas
cards.teaser: A jury found a Catholic priest guilty of sexually abusing women under his spiritual care, prompting a Louisiana chapel to remove his name.
cards.body:
A jury convicted a Catholic priest of sexual assault against women he provided spiritual guidance to in Texas. The priest, identified in reports as Father Odiong, was found guilty after a trial in which a woman testified he justified sexual contact as spiritual and holy. She said she felt ashamed by the encounters.

Following the conviction, a chapel in Louisiana that the priest built removed his name from the facility. OSV News and Crux reported that questions remain for several church leaders regarding their oversight of the case.

cards.headline: Film editor Marcia Lucas dies at 80
cards.teaser: The Oscar-winning editor and former wife of George Lucas, who worked on the original Star Wars trilogy, has died.
cards.body:
Marcia Lucas, an Oscar-winning film editor, has died at age 80. She was recognized as a crucial creative force behind the original Star Wars trilogy, shaping films that became defining cultural landmarks.

Lucas was the former wife of director George Lucas. Her editing work on the space trilogy earned her widespread acclaim and an Academy Award for her contributions to cinema.

cards.headline: Trump criticizes artists withdrawing from US Freedom 250 concert
cards.teaser: The president responded to performers who pulled out of the event, citing concerns it would be political, and suggested he might appear himself.
cards.body:
President Trump has criticized performers who withdrew from the US Freedom 250 concert, including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride. The artists cited concerns that the event would have a political nature.

In response to the withdrawals, Trump suggested he might appear or perform at the concert himself, intensifying the public dispute over the event's character.

hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explosion damages launch pad, delays operations
hero.body:
A New Glenn rocket owned by Blue Origin exploded during a test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night, destroying the launchpad and creating a massive fireball visible across the region. The explosion occurred at 9pm ET during a scheduled "hotfire" test at Launch Complex 36, with an orange sky visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away.

The incident poses a significant threat to NASA's lunar exploration timeline. Blue Origin had recently won a contract to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of NASA's $20 billion moon base. The explosion raises questions about whether the company can meet these commitments.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed that all employees were safe and uninjured. He described the day as "very rough" but committed to rebuilding and resuming operations. The company called the incident "an anomaly" and said it was already investigating the root cause.

NASA administrator Jared Isaacman acknowledged the setback in a post on X, stating that spaceflight is "unforgiving" and that developing new heavy-lift launch capability is "extraordinarily difficult." He announced that NASA would conduct a full evaluation of mission timelines following the explosion and work with partners to investigate the incident and assess its impact on the Artemis and Moon Base programs.

The shockwaves from the explosion were felt across Florida's space coast, with residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reporting that their homes shook. People in South Carolina, hundreds of miles north, reported seeing a glow in the sky. Flames continued burning at the launchpad more than two hours after the explosion, though emergency officials said there was no threat from fumes or other hazards.

This explosion represents the latest in a series of setbacks for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for NASA contracts. Last month, a payload from New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. The FAA cleared it to return to flight last week, making Thursday's test the first static fire test since that clearance.

Blue Origin is competing with SpaceX to provide lunar landers for NASA's Artemis program. Artemis III, scheduled for 2027, will test Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander alongside SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System to determine which will carry astronauts to the lunar surface in Artemis IV, planned for 2028. This would mark the first crewed lunar landing since 1972.

Elon Musk, owner of SpaceX and X, commented briefly on the explosion, saying "Most unfortunate" and noting that "Rockets are hard."

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempts to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight was diverted to Wisconsin and a passenger detained following multiple attempts to reach the cockpit.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin after a passenger made multiple attempts to breach the cockpit. Crew members reported the disruption, prompting the emergency landing. Law enforcement detained the unruly passenger upon arrival.

The incident caused travel disruptions for passengers aboard the flight, who later continued to their original destination after the diversion.

cards.headline: SpaceX prepares $80 billion IPO with most shares already allocated
cards.teaser: SpaceX is planning an initial public offering valued at $80 billion, but the majority of shares have already been committed to specific buyers.
cards.body:
SpaceX is proceeding with an $80 billion IPO, though 78 percent of the offering has already been allocated to existing investors, significantly limiting shares available to retail buyers. The company revealed in its IPO filing that government contracts already represent one-fifth of its 2025 revenue, including a recent $6.45 billion Space Force contract award.

The structure creates a challenging situation for Wall Street firms, which risk losing future business if they don't participate, while their clients face limited upside potential given the high valuation and pre-sold shares. This mirrors a broader trend of technology companies going public at valuations that offer minimal room for post-IPO gains.

cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotechnology industry expands rapidly.

cards.headline: Freight broker removes carriers based on safety scores after Supreme Court ruling
cards.teaser: C.H. Robinson has begun removing carriers from its network based on safety scores, a move that follows a recent Supreme Court decision on broker liability.
cards.body:
Transportation and logistics company C.H. Robinson is removing carriers from its network based on their safety performance scores. The decision follows a Supreme Court ruling in Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II that clarified broker responsibilities in the transportation chain.

The ruling addressed liability standards for freight brokers without expanding shipper liability. Industry observers view the decision as potentially transformative for trucking safety standards, prompting companies like C.H. Robinson to reassess their carrier selection criteria.

cards.headline: High IPO valuations for tech companies leave little upside for retail investors
cards.teaser: Companies valued as richly as SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic before going public have historically offered poor returns for ordinary investors.
cards.body:
When newly public companies enter the market at premium valuations—like SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic are expected to—ordinary investors face poor investment prospects. The richly valued IPOs leave minimal room for gains after shares become available to the public.

This pricing dynamic means that early private investors and company insiders capture most of the value gains before retail investors have a chance to participate. The trend reflects how value distribution has shifted in technology investing.

cards.headline: Schneider Electric uses AI to boost worker productivity rather than cut jobs
cards.teaser: French manufacturing company Schneider Electric deployed artificial intelligence to make existing workers more productive instead of replacing them.
cards.body:
Schneider Electric, a French multinational corporation, implemented artificial intelligence in its manufacturing operations with a focus on enhancing worker capabilities rather than eliminating positions. The approach contrasts with many companies that have used automation primarily to reduce headcount.

The company integrated AI tools into production processes to assist workers with tasks and decision-making. The strategy aims to increase output and efficiency while maintaining employment levels. Schneider Electric's model offers an alternative path for companies considering AI adoption in manufacturing settings.

hero.headline: Microsoft threatens legal action against security researcher for disclosing exploits
hero.body:
Microsoft has warned a security researcher with potential legal action after publicly releasing multiple zero-day vulnerabilities without first coordinating with the company. The researcher, known online as Nightmare Eclipse, disclosed six zero-day exploits publicly, along with proof-of-concept code.

The confrontation has reignited debate within the cybersecurity community about responsible vulnerability disclosure. Microsoft contacted the researcher and raised the possibility of a criminal investigation in response to what the company characterized as uncoordinated disclosure of security vulnerabilities. Some posts from the researcher suggest they may be a disgruntled former employee, though this remains unclear.

Microsoft typically prefers that security researchers report vulnerabilities privately through coordinated disclosure processes. This approach gives the company time to develop and distribute patches before vulnerability information becomes public, protecting users from potential attacks. The researcher, however, has described feeling humiliated by Microsoft's response and has pledged what they called a "bone shattering drop," suggesting additional vulnerability releases may be forthcoming.

Zero-day vulnerabilities are security flaws that software makers do not yet know about and for which no patch exists. Public disclosure of such vulnerabilities before fixes are available can leave users exposed to exploitation. The timing and nature of disclosure has long been contentious among researchers, companies, and security experts.

Microsoft has established formal channels for security researchers to report vulnerabilities responsibly, including a bug bounty program offering financial rewards. The company argues that coordinated disclosure protects users by allowing adequate time to develop, test, and distribute security updates before attackers can exploit newly revealed flaws.

The dispute highlights ongoing tensions in cybersecurity over disclosure practices and ethics. Some researchers contend that public disclosure serves the public interest by forcing companies to address security issues more quickly. Companies generally maintain that uncoordinated disclosure puts users at risk and can violate computer fraud laws in certain jurisdictions.

Security researcher Kevin Beaumont drew attention to how Microsoft has handled this particular situation, sparking broader criticism of the company's response. The incident has generated coverage across major technology and cybersecurity publications, with commentators questioning whether Microsoft's legal threats represent an appropriate response to uncoordinated vulnerability disclosure.

The specific technical details of the six disclosed vulnerabilities have not been detailed in available reporting. Microsoft has not publicly confirmed whether patches for these issues have been developed or distributed. The company also has not released statements regarding the severity of the vulnerabilities or their potential impact on users.

This confrontation underscores the complex relationship between technology companies and independent security researchers, where questions about disclosure timing, legal responsibility, and public safety remain unresolved.

cards.headline: Nvidia-powered Windows PCs set to launch next week
cards.teaser: The first Windows computers running Nvidia processors will be announced at an upcoming event.
cards.body:
Nvidia is preparing to announce its first Windows-based personal computers powered by its own processors. The unveiling is expected next week, according to reporting from Axios.

Nvidia, Microsoft, and chip designer Arm have all posted cryptic social media messages ahead of the event. The new processors are reportedly called N1X and are designed for laptop computers. This marks Nvidia's move into the PC processor market, expanding beyond its traditional focus on graphics cards.

cards.headline: Google rolls out Gemini Spark AI assistant to premium subscribers
cards.teaser: Google's new automated AI tool handles tasks like inbox summaries and event planning.
cards.body:
Google has launched Gemini Spark, a 24/7 AI assistant available to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the United States. The tool automates everyday tasks like summarizing email inboxes and planning local events by continuously accessing various aspects of a user's digital life.

According to early testing, Gemini Spark proves useful for these automation functions. Google chose to release it as a standalone product rather than integrate it into existing Gemini features.

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot switches to token-based billing
cards.teaser: Microsoft's AI coding assistant has changed its pricing model, prompting developer complaints.
cards.body:
GitHub has introduced a new token-based billing system for Copilot, its AI-powered coding assistant owned by Microsoft. The change has generated criticism from developers who use the service.

The shift away from the previous pricing structure marks what some observers are calling the end of a golden age for the product. Token-based billing charges users based on the amount of AI-generated content they request, rather than a flat subscription fee. Developers have expressed consternation over the new pricing approach, though specific details about rate increases or cost comparisons were not provided in available reporting.

cards.headline: Meta developing AI-powered wearable pendant
cards.teaser: The social media company is expanding its AI hardware offerings beyond glasses and headsets.
cards.body:
Meta is reportedly developing an AI-powered pendant as part of its expansion into AI hardware products. The device would complement Meta's existing consumer electronics lineup, which already includes virtual reality headsets and AI-integrated smart glasses.

The company continues to make significant investments in artificial intelligence technology and hardware development as a key part of its business strategy.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels investment fund
cards.teaser: Twenty Snap alumni have created a fund focused on backing social media startups.
cards.body:
Twenty former Snap employees have created Ghost Angels, a new investment fund dedicated to backing early-stage social media companies. The fund name references Snap's iconic ghost mascot and logo.

The alumni group is pooling their resources to identify and support the next generation of social media ventures, leveraging their collective experience from working at the photo-sharing platform.

cards.headline: Venture capitalists discuss AI investment trends
cards.teaser: Three prominent investors shared views on artificial intelligence funding during a panel discussion.
cards.body:
Three top venture capital investors discussed the current state of AI investment at a recent event. One investor joked about the intense competition for young founders building AI companies.

The investor suggested that 22-year-old founders in San Francisco working on AI projects might receive seed funding term sheets, while 19-year-old founders could attract Series A investment offers. The comment was made half-jokingly but reflected the heightened interest in AI startups among venture capital firms. The panel addressed what was described as an AI frenzy in the startup funding environment.

hero.headline: PSG retain Champions League title after penalty shootout win over Arsenal
hero.body:
Paris Saint-Germain won their second consecutive Champions League title, defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout in Budapest. The match ended 1-1 after extra time, with PSG ultimately prevailing in the decisive moment.

Arsenal took the lead through Kai Havertz, who scored in the opening stages of the match. The striker, who has previous experience winning major finals, struck from a tight angle on the left side of the six-yard box after reacting quickly to a loose ball. His powerful shot found the top corner, leaving PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov unable to respond.

PSG equalised through Ousmane Dembélé from the penalty spot in the 65th minute after Cristhian Mosquera was adjudged to have committed a handball offence. The equaliser sparked an intense final period, with both teams creating opportunities but neither able to find a winning goal.

Arsenal's manager Mikel Arteta had prioritised defensive solidity, selecting a back four composed of centre-halves and defensive midfielders. The strategy worked effectively in the first half, with Arsenal pressing high and limiting PSG's attacking threat. However, PSG gradually improved as the match progressed.

When the teams could not be separated after extra time, the contest went to a penalty shootout. Arsenal substitute Eberechi Eze missed in the second round, but goalkeeper David Raya kept Arsenal alive by saving from Nuno Mendes in the third round.

Gabriel Magalhães, Arsenal's defensive leader, was given the responsibility of taking the final penalty of the regulation five rounds. Under intense pressure, Gabriel went for power but sent his attempt high over the crossbar. The miss proved decisive, handing PSG victory and ending Arsenal's hopes of claiming their first Champions League title.

The defeat came just days after Arsenal had won the Premier League for the first time in 22 years, a drought that had defined the club's recent history. That league triumph had represented a significant moment for the club and its supporters, making this Champions League final loss particularly painful.

PSG's back-to-back titles cement their status among European football's elite. Few clubs have managed to retain the Champions League trophy in consecutive years since the competition was rebranded in 1992. The achievement represents the culmination of significant investment in building a squad capable of winning European club football's most prestigious trophy.

For Arsenal, the loss represents a missed opportunity to add European glory to their domestic success. Despite a well-organised defensive approach and positive moments in attack, they fell short in the final hurdle. Gabriel's missed penalty will be remembered as the defining moment that separated the two sides.

cards.headline: Defending champion Coco Gauff eliminated from French Open
cards.teaser: Coco Gauff lost in the third round to Anastasia Potapova, ending her title defense at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Coco Gauff's title defense at the French Open has ended in the third round, following a loss to Anastasia Potapova. The American was unable to extend her reign as women's champion at Roland Garros.

Gauff's early exit from the tournament marks a significant upset in the women's draw, as the reigning champion failed to advance beyond the opening week of competition.

cards.headline: Scotland's Billy Gilmour ruled out of World Cup with knee injury
cards.teaser: Midfielder Billy Gilmour will miss the World Cup after sustaining a knee injury in a friendly match against Curacao.
cards.body:
Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour has been ruled out of the World Cup after sustaining a knee injury during Saturday's 4-1 friendly victory over Curaçao.

Despite the convincing win, which saw Scotland play against 10 men for much of the match, the injury dampened what had been an encouraging performance ahead of the tournament. Manchester United's Fletcher has been mentioned as a potential replacement for Gilmour in Scotland's squad for the World Cup.

cards.headline: Northampton Saints secure home semifinal with last-second win over Gloucester
cards.teaser: George Furbank scored a try in the final moments to give Saints a home playoff semifinal.
cards.body:
George Furbank scored a dramatic last-gasp try to secure a home semifinal for Northampton Saints in the Premiership playoffs. The decisive moment came in an 11-try thriller against Gloucester, ensuring Saints will host their semifinal match.

The high-scoring encounter between the two sides featured back-and-forth action throughout, ultimately decided by Furbank's crucial late score.

cards.headline: New Zealand's Mitchell Santner returns for England Test series
cards.teaser: All-rounder Mitchell Santner rejoins the New Zealand squad for the Test matches starting at Lord's.
cards.body:
New Zealand received a boost with the return of all-rounder Mitchell Santner for the Test series against England. The series begins at Lord's on Thursday.

Santner's inclusion strengthens New Zealand's options across both batting and bowling as they prepare for the opening Test match in London.

cards.headline: Pentagon requires troops to meet fitness standards for White House UFC event
cards.teaser: Military personnel must meet weight and fitness criteria to attend a UFC fight at the White House.
cards.body:
The Pentagon is recruiting troops to attend a UFC fight at the White House, with attendance requiring soldiers to meet specific fitness standards. Memos show that troops must meet weight requirements to receive free tickets to the event.

The fitness criteria include meeting established weight and height standards. The requirements apply to military personnel seeking to attend the White House event.

cards.headline: Florida baseball to face Miami with schedule change
cards.teaser: The Gators will play Miami on Saturday night at 8 p.m. in the Gainesville Regional.
cards.body:
Florida will take on Miami on Saturday at 8 p.m. in the Gainesville Regional after advancing past Rider with a walk-off victory. The matchup sets up an in-state rivalry clash in the next round of the regional tournament.

Coach Kevin O'Sullivan praised his team's resilience following the Rider win, noting how the Gators battled back in that contest. Florida now shifts focus to preparing for the Hurricanes in what promises to be a competitive regional matchup.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor whose work shaped the original Star Wars trilogy, died at age 80. Lucasfilm announced her death Saturday.

Lucas won an Academy Award for her editing work on the original Star Wars film in 1977. Her contributions extended beyond the franchise that made her famous, as she worked on multiple films during Hollywood's creative renaissance of the 1970s and early 1980s.

She was formerly married to Star Wars creator George Lucas. The pair divorced in the 1980s, but her influence on the original trilogy remained a subject of discussion among film historians and fans for decades.

Lucasfilm released a tribute following the announcement of her death. The statement recognized her role in the creation of the Star Wars films that launched one of the most successful franchises in entertainment history.

Marcia Lucas's editing shaped key sequences in the original Star Wars, including the film's climactic Death Star battle. Film editors have credited her work with helping establish the pacing and emotional resonance that distinguished the original trilogy.

Her career in film editing began in the early 1970s. She worked alongside other editors and directors during a period of significant change in American cinema, contributing to films that would define a generation of moviegoers.

The news of her death prompted responses across the film industry. Former colleagues and film professionals acknowledged her contributions to cinema and her role in creating some of the most memorable moments in movie history.

Marcia Lucas retired from film editing decades ago. She maintained a private life away from the public attention that followed the Star Wars franchise and its continued expansion.

cards.headline: Kelly Curtis, Actress and Sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, Dies at 69
cards.teaser: Kelly Curtis, an American actress known for The Sentinel and sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, died at her home.
cards.body: Jamie Lee Curtis wrote that her older sister passed away in her home in nature and at peace. Kelly Curtis appeared in films including The Sentinel and worked as an actress during her career.

cards.headline: Multiple Artists Drop Out of Trump-Backed Freedom 250 Concert
cards.teaser: Several performers withdrew from government-sponsored Freedom 250 concerts in Washington after initially committing to appear.
cards.body:
Martina McBride, the Commodores, Bret Michaels, and Young MC withdrew from performances at the Freedom 250 concert series, expressing concerns that the events would be political despite being presented as nonpartisan.

In response, President Trump posted multiple messages on Truth Social criticizing the departing artists and announcing he would replace the concert series with an "America Is Back" rally on Wednesday. Trump suggested he would perform himself and stated that only great patriots would be invited to the event.

cards.headline: Spurs Force Game 7 Against Thunder in NBA Western Conference Final
cards.teaser: San Antonio routed Oklahoma City 118-91 in Game 6 to set up a winner-take-all matchup in the conference final.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 118-91 in Game 6 of the NBA Western Conference Final on Thursday night, forcing a decisive Game 7. Victor Wembanyama paced the Spurs with 28 points in the victory.

The win set up a winner-take-all matchup after the series had remained competitive through the first five games.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Open to Mentoring Next Spider-Man Actor
cards.teaser: The actor told Empire magazine he would like to help set up whoever takes over the Marvel franchise.
cards.body:
Tom Holland recently told Empire magazine that he's excited about handing over the Spider-Man role to the next actor. He envisions himself playing a mentoring role similar to what Robert Downey Jr. provided when Holland first joined the Marvel franchise.

Holland mentioned several possibilities for who could take on the mantle next, including Miles Morales, Spider-Gwen, and Spider-Woman. He's eager to help set up whoever becomes the next face of the Spider-Man franchise.

cards.headline: Pete Davidson Praises Ex-Girlfriend Kim Kardashian in Podcast Appearance
cards.teaser: The comedian called Kardashian superhuman during a conversation with Nikki Glaser nearly four years after their split.
cards.body:
Pete Davidson spoke positively about his former girlfriend Kim Kardashian during a podcast with Nikki Glaser. He described the reality television star and businesswoman as superhuman.

Davidson praised Kardashian's acting career in his comments. The two dated and split almost four years ago, and Davidson rarely discusses their past relationship publicly.

cards.headline: Hannah Waddingham Says She Never Auditioned for Wicked Role
cards.teaser: The actress confirmed she did not try out for the part of Madame Morrible in the musical film.
cards.body:
Hannah Waddingham addressed speculation about her involvement in the Wicked film adaptation. She confirmed that she never auditioned for the role of Madame Morrible.

The statement shut down rumors that had circulated about Waddingham being considered for the part. She made the clarification after reports suggested she had been in contention for the role in the movie musical.

hero.headline: Trump calls court system rigged after rulings block tariffs and Kennedy Center renaming
hero.body:
Trump wrote on Truth Social that the court system is rigged, comparing it unfavorably to the judicial systems in other countries. The statement came after courts ruled against a key part of his economic policy and blocked the addition of his name to the Kennedy Center.

The rulings represent setbacks for the administration's agenda. One decision halted implementation of tariff policies that Trump had described as central to his economic plans. The other stopped the renaming of the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts to include the president's name.

Trump's criticism of the judiciary echoes previous statements he has made about courts that rule against his policies. The president has repeatedly questioned the impartiality of judges who issue unfavorable decisions.

The tariff ruling affects trade policy that the administration had sought to implement as part of its broader economic strategy. The court found legal issues with how the tariffs were being imposed, though Trump maintained the policies were necessary for American economic interests.

The Kennedy Center decision addressed efforts to rename the Washington cultural institution. The venue has hosted performances and events since 1971 and is named after President John F. Kennedy. Courts blocked the proposed name change.

White House Communications Director Steven Cheung has defended the president's policies in other matters, calling criticism of administration decisions fake news. The administration has not yet announced whether it will appeal either ruling.

The decisions add to a series of legal challenges the administration has faced in implementing its policy priorities. Federal courts have acted as a check on executive actions across multiple policy areas.

Trump characterized the rulings as evidence of bias in the judicial system. He argued that courts were preventing him from fulfilling campaign promises to voters. Legal experts note that judicial review of executive actions is a standard part of the constitutional system of checks and balances.

cards.headline: Trump plans rally for America's 250th anniversary after artists withdraw from state fair
cards.teaser: President Trump announced he will hold a political rally to mark the nation's 250th anniversary after several performers pulled out of the Great American State Fair.
cards.body:
President Trump announced plans to hold an "America Is Back" rally on Wednesday to replace a concert series for America's 250th anniversary celebration. The rally comes after several performers withdrew from the Great American State Fair event scheduled for the National Mall.

Trump made the announcement in a series of posts to his Truth Social account on Saturday, along with other statements about his administration's efforts on the National Mall and responses to recent court decisions. The rally will serve as an alternative to the musical performances that were originally planned as part of the anniversary celebrations.

cards.headline: White House denies report that Wiles advised Vance to take social media break
cards.teaser: The White House rejected a New York Times report claiming chief of staff Susie Wiles told Vice President Vance to step back from social media.
cards.body:
The White House denied a New York Times report claiming that chief of staff Susie Wiles advised Vice President Vance to reduce his social media presence. White House Communications Director Steven Cheung dismissed the story as "complete fake news" in a post on X.

Cheung's response directly contradicted the Times' allegation that Wiles had recommended Vance take a break from posting on social media platforms.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth softens China rhetoric at Singapore conference
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth moderated his tone on China while speaking to Pacific leaders weeks after President Trump met with Chinese officials in Beijing.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth adopted a more moderate tone on China during his remarks at the Shangri-La Dialogue conference in Singapore, a shift occurring weeks after President Trump's bilateral summit in Beijing. While acknowledging "rightful alarm" over China's military buildup, Hegseth notably avoided discussing Taiwan in his address to Pacific leaders and diplomats.

Hegseth urged Asian allies to increase their military spending and take on greater responsibility for regional security. His balanced approach reflected an effort to manage U.S.-China relations while encouraging greater burden-sharing among America's regional partners against emerging threats.

cards.headline: Rep. Mace says she has no regrets about Epstein files vote after Trump backs primary opponent
cards.teaser: Rep. Nancy Mace said she does not regret voting to release Jeffrey Epstein files, even after President Trump endorsed her challenger in the South Carolina governor race.
cards.body:
Rep. Nancy Mace said she stands by her decision to vote for releasing files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. She made the statement after President Trump endorsed her opponent in the upcoming Republican primary for South Carolina governor.

Mace wrote on social media that she voted to release the Epstein files and has no regrets about the decision. Trump's endorsement of her challenger came after Mace's vote on the files.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayoral candidate Pratt rejects Trump endorsement
cards.teaser: Spencer Pratt said he does not need President Trump's endorsement in the Los Angeles mayor race, calling it a local election separate from national politics.
cards.body:
Los Angeles mayoral candidate Spencer Pratt said he does not want an endorsement from President Trump, stating that national politics should stay out of local elections. Pratt told NBC News that he only needs endorsement from mothers, who he said will get him elected.

The former reality star emphasized that his race is local and he does not care about national political developments. Trump had backed Pratt's candidacy for mayor of Los Angeles.

cards.headline: Giants quarterback Dart defends introducing Trump at rally
cards.teaser: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart said he introduced President Trump at a rally out of patriotism, not partisanship, after facing criticism.
cards.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart defended his decision to introduce President Trump at a New York rally. Dart said he viewed it as an opportunity to introduce the President of the United States and acted out of love for his country.

Dart said his thinking was simple when given the opportunity. He characterized the appearance as patriotic rather than political, responding to criticism of his participation in the event.
